Problem world. In the model, microbes can transfer from a surface to the hands and then from the hands to the mouth if the hands are not cleaned. Correct washing with soap and water greatly reduces the number of microbes on the hands, without meaning that every microbe in the world disappears. To reduce risk, we can break the transmission chain at several points.

Case data. after the observation “the observed problem exists, but its cause has not yet been located”, both hypotheses remain possible: H1: transmission is through hands and H2: transmission is direct through food. We can make one additional observation.

Question. What is the minimum information that would separate the hypotheses? Explain why a shared observation does not help, while a discriminating one does.

Problem world. In this model, a source produces sound when it vibrates. The vibration sets the surrounding medium in motion, and the variations reach a receiver. A larger vibration can produce a louder sound under comparable conditions; distance and obstacles can reduce what reaches the receiver. We do not confuse the sound source with the receiver that detects it.

Case data. after the observation “the observed problem exists, but its cause has not yet been located”, both hypotheses remain possible: H1: the source does not vibrate and H2: the receiver is defect. We can make one additional observation.

Question. What is the minimum information that would separate the hypotheses? Explain why a shared observation does not help, while a discriminating one does.

Problem world. In the model, a magnet can attract certain magnetic materials without direct contact. Two magnet ends can attract or repel depending on orientation. We do not assume that all metals are magnetic; the result of the test is stated explicitly for every object. A thin nonmagnetic barrier does not necessarily stop the magnet’s effect in our model.

Case data. after the observation “the observed problem exists, but its cause has not yet been located”, both hypotheses remain possible: H1: the object is not magnetic and H2: the magnet is too far. We can make one additional observation.

Question. What is the minimum information that would separate the hypotheses? Explain why a shared observation does not help, while a discriminating one does.

Problem world. In the teaching model, foods can provide energy and substances needed to build and operate the body. A balanced meal is not decided by a single food but by the combination and amount. For this problem, each option has explicitly stated properties; no real food values need to be memorized. We track three requirements at the same time: enough energy, a source of protein, and a source of fiber.

Case data. after the observation “the observed problem exists, but its cause has not yet been located”, both hypotheses remain possible: H1: the lack of satiety comes from a portion with too little energy and H2: the lack comes from unsuitable composition. We can make one additional observation.

Question. What is the minimum information that would separate the hypotheses? Explain why a shared observation does not help, while a discriminating one does.

Problem world. A measurement is useful only if we know what quantity was measured and in which unit. For comparisons, values must be expressed in the same unit and obtained by the same method. Repeating a measurement can show whether an unusual result is stable or only an accidental error. No conversions need to be memorized in this problem; every required conversion is stated explicitly.

Case data. After the observation “the unusual value exists, but its cause has not yet been identified,” both hypotheses remain possible: H1: the unusual value is a random error; H2: the instrument is misadjusted. We can make one additional observation.

Question. What is the minimum information that would separate the hypotheses? Explain why a shared observation does not help, while a discriminating one does.

Rules. A coalition is winning if the sum of its members’ seats reaches the threshold. Minimal winning means it is winning but removing any member makes it lose.

Task. Which coalitions are minimal winning coalitions?
